judged_text: Dead fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-256 and 312-315) — in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares a non-null string to a falsy value and can never match, always evaluating to undefined; bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings, or new bookings created via the no-credentialId path in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents) will send calendarId: undefined to the Google API on reschedule/cancel, causing update/delete failures and orphaned calendar events.

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback branch is logically dead: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` (and the analogous `calendarId` in delete) runs the `.find(...)` only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` (string) to a falsy value (null/undefined) and will never match, yielding `undefined`. The diff does not show any subsequent guaranteed fallback to a valid calendarId in update/delete, and even if a later `|| "primary"` exists, this change would incorrectly target the wrong calendar for events created on a non-primary destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing (legacy refs), leading to update/delete failures or orphaned events.
